result:
If I could change the world in one way, I’d make empathy the default human instinct — not just toward people we know and love, but toward strangers, rivals, and even future generations.

So many of the world’s problems — conflict, inequality, environmental destruction — come from a failure to fully feel the weight of another’s experience. If we instinctively understood the pain we cause and the joy we can share, we’d build systems more gently, govern more wisely, and treat the planet as a home rather than a resource.

One change can’t solve everything. But a world wired for empathy would make every other change more possible.
